subject: Re: Rate bridge request and competitor pricing details
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@halohealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Claire O'Neill <coleen@halohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Rate review + competitive pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the time today. As discussed, Halo Health is consolidating our LLM spend and we need a concrete rate comparison to present to procurement. We ran a quick vendor sweep and have the following baseline pricing that the committee expects to at least match or beat:

- OpenAI (gpt-4o-mini): $0.015 / 1k prompt tokens, $0.03 / 1k completion tokens, streaming supported
- Anthropic (claude-3-mini): $0.018 / 1k prompt, $0.025 / 1k completion
- Together (gptj-16k): $0.012 / 1k prompt+completion unified
- AWS Bedrock (small): $0.02 / 1k prompt, $0.02 / 1k completion (volume tiers apply)

Halo's expected monthly baseline: ~120M tokens (mixed p/c), with spikes up to 300M on campaign days. Primary use: clinical triage workflows + patient-facing summarization (latency sensitivity).

Key asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood match the per-1k token economics above for hosted API? If not exact match, what is the closest flat rate you can offer for a 12-month committed spend?
- Are there specific SLAs for latency on short requests (<=250 tokens)?
- Any credits or onboarding discounts for a first-year committed contract?

I attached a one-page rate request and our baseline usage spreadsheet. Procurement wants a fully-burdened hosted price (tokens + any per-request fees) to compare apples-to-apples.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
Halo Health

Attachments: Halo_Rate_Request_2026.xlsx

- Any data residency or encryption requirements beyond standard SOC2 / TLS?

Prelim note: based on the usage you shared, we can approach the Together/OpenAI bands with a committed 12-month contract if Halo agrees to a modest committed spend cadence and a small onboarding credit. I will pull a few concrete options and loop in Karthik for commercial approval. Expect a formal proposal by end of week.

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Halo Health - rate sweep attached (need quick guidance)

Karthik / Vivek —

Forwarding Samir's note and their baseline sheet. Key numbers they pulled are in message 1. Their ask: match or beat Together/OpenAI band on hosted API. Usage looks steady ~120M tokens/mo but spikes to 300M. Latency matters for triage (<=250 tokens).

My thinking (options to present):
1) Committed 12-month tier: $0.012 / 1k tokens flat (hosted) for first 100M, $0.010 / 1k above — requires 12-mo commit ~ $X/month (I calculated a back-of-envelope commitment at $14k/mo). Include 1 month onboarding credit.
2) Reserved + burst: Reserved baseline at $0.015 / 1k for guaranteed pool (covers 120M), burst pricing $0.018 / 1k up to peak — better for them operationally but higher unit cost when spiking.
3) No-commit list: $0.020 / 1k prompt$0.028 / 1k completion (our standard public hosted levels) — only if they refuse commit.

I want to push option 1 but need greenlight to offer $0.012 in a commercial proposal. Also need to confirm we can commit to a 99.9% latency SLO for <=250 token calls in hosted (we won't provide hard SLA for median but will provide percentiles and a commercial SLA for uptime).

Attachments: Halo_Rate_Request_2026.xlsx (from Samir)

Thoughts?
- Vanessa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Halo Health - rate sweep attached (need quick guidance)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the write-up. My guidance:
- Approve option 1 as a negotiable anchor, but tie the $0.012 / 1k to a minimum committed spend: 100M tokens/mo equivalent for 12 months (or an upfront equivalent prepay). If they want true 120M baseline, price accordingly (we shouldn't over-index).
- Offer 1 month onboarding credit (waive first month of committed charge) and a one-time migration credit of $15k if they sign within 30 days — this will be accounted for in pricing approvals.
- For the latency ask: do not promise numeric latency percentiles in the commercial contract beyond standard availability SLA (99.9%). Instead offer a latency performance attachment: monthly latency reports, prioritized routing, and a playbook for burst capacity. That mitigates risk and avoids hard latency SLO exposure.
- Commercial approval: I can sign off on $0.012 if finance prep a 12-mo commitment schedule (legal needs the deal team to submit redlines through the usual channel).

Send a proposal with those guardrails and a DocuSign-ready term sheet. I can escalate to finance for a one-time exception on the migration credit.

- Karthik

Subject: Redwood proposal: 12-month committed hosted pricing (Halo Health)

Samir / Claire —

Thanks again for patience while we ran numbers. Attached is a short commercial summary and a rate worksheet that maps your baseline spreadsheet to three practical packaging options. High level:

Option A — 12-month committed (recommended)
- Unit: $0.012 / 1k tokens (hosted, fully-burdened) for up to 120M tokens/month; $0.010 / 1k thereafter.
- Onboarding: 1 month onboarding credit (first month waived).
- Migration credit: $15,000 one-time (conditional on signature within 30 days).
- SLA: 99.9% availability. Monthly latency report and prioritized routing for triage flows (we will not commit to numeric latency SLAs in the MSA; performance attachment provided).

Option B — Reserved baseline + burst
- Reserved pool: $0.015 / 1k tokens for reserved baseline (recommended if Halo prefers predictable pool).
- Burst: $0.018 / 1k for traffic above reserved pool.

Option C — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- Public hosted list: $0.020 / 1k prompt, $0.028 / 1k completion.

Next steps: if Option A looks good we will send a one-page term sheet and DocuSign link. Please confirm target start date (we typically allow 30–45 days for provisioning + migration).

Attached: Halo_Rate_Request_2026.xlsx, Halo_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW)

Thanks —
